newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue bullrun on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue bullrun on Monday.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares rose one percent to new highs on Monday but some brokers said they expected it to slow down a little amidst some profit-taking ahead of the national budget announcement on Thursday.
The main industrial index leapt 135.15 points -- or 1.2 percent -- to break through the 11,500 pyschological mark and close at a new all time peak of 11,541.60.
"Today was another strong move but I think we might see a bit of profit-taking later in the week and we might see the market stabilise around current levels before the budget," one broker said.

Some market analysts however said they expected the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) to defy traditional trends and keep on a firm path ahead of the budget which they said market players expected to be positive.
On the exchange on Monday, hotels, supermarkets and beverages conglomerate Delta jumped 70 cents up to 2,100, merchant banker NMB rose 20 cents to 3,525 and Alloys gained 10 cents to 310.
The mining board continued dull with Wankie Colliery adding 10 cents to 590 while nickel producer Bindura shed 20 cents to 580.
The mining index lost 6.94 points to 833.24.
